title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 60
paragraphs: These, then, came on shouting and in confused numbers, thinking to make short work of the Greeks. Pausanias, when the cavalry began to attack, sent a horseman to the Athenians and said: “Athenians, now that the greatest contest is set before us — one whose outcome is the freedom or slavery of Greece — we, the Lacedaemonians, and you, the Athenians, have been deserted by our allies, who have run away during the past night. Now, therefore, it is determined what we must do about this: we must defend ourselves and protect one another as best we may. If the cavalry had set out to attack you first, we and the Tegeans (who with us refuse to betray the cause of Greece) would have been bound to go to your aid; but as it is, since the whole body has come against us, it is right that you should come to that portion of the army which is hardest pressed, to give aid. However, if something has befallen you that makes it impossible to come help, do us a kindness by sending the archers to us. We know that you have been by far the most zealous in this present war, so we trust you will listen to this request too.”
